answer.reason: The verses state two chief deeds of Artaxerxes: his letter that stopped the Jerusalem work, and his decree sending Ezra with royal support.

clauses.english: sent a letter that made the building of Jerusalem cease
clauses.quote: made them to cease by force and power

clauses.english: gave Ezra a decree to go up to Jerusalem, with silver and supplies from the king's treasury
clauses.quote: I make a decree, that all they of the people of Israel

doubts: EZR 4:7 and 4:11 only mention letters written to him, so they are not cited.
EZR 4:21-22 sits in a gap between shown verses, and its speaker is inferred from 4:23 naming Artaxerxes' letter.
The Nehemiah verses (2:1, 5:14, 13:6) only date events by his reign, and the cupbearer scene's outcome is not given, so I left them out.
